content.text: The verifier's feedback again affirms every element of the analysis and identifies the only failure as the `audit frequency limited` deterministic check, which it expressly characterises as explainable heuristic noise where no audit clause exists. There is no substantive defect to repair, and proposing a redline would be wrong for a compliant finding — inserting frequency/notice/cost language would manufacture an audit obligation against our own client. Re-submitting with the rationale stated as tightly as possible.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: This rule constrains audit rights exercisable against us, and the Agreement grants Kubient none. Searches for "audit", "records", "inspect" and "verif" return no hits, and a paragraph-by-paragraph read of the single section confirms it: §5 Fees and Payment (p0023) creates no examination or true-up right, and the only access-related obligation on AP (§1, p0001) is cooperation so Kubient can deliver the Services, not a right to examine AP's books, usage or systems. With no audit right in Kubient's favour there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access term to constrain, so the position is at least as protective as the preferred standard (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor cost, no system access). Compliant is correct rather than "missing": treating it as missing would require inserting an audit obligation against our own party, which the rule does not seek. The "audit frequency limited" deterministic check necessarily fails where no audit clause exists and is heuristic noise, not evidence of a gap. No redline or counterparty comment is proposed. Parked under the reporting/revenue-verification rule to avoid double-flagging: Impressions are measured solely as measured by Kubient (p0009) and revenue share runs through the Exhibits with no AP-side verification right — a point that runs in our favour to fix.
